previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a 58-year-old male with a history of acute myeloid leukemia in remission, chronic systolic heart failure (LVEF 25%), and chronic kidney disease, was admitted for acute nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, and fever following potential exposure to family with gastroenteritis. He presented with dehydration, hypotension, and acute kidney injury with metabolic acidosis. Initial management included IV fluid resuscitation and empiric antibiotics. His course was complicated by pulmonary edema on hospital day 3, requiring IV furosemide. Diarrhea improved with loperamide, psyllium, and cholestyramine. Stool testing later confirmed rotavirus. Renal function improved with hydration, and he was discharged euvolemic, off oxygen, with instructions to restart furosemide when diarrhea resolved and to follow up with nephrology for ongoing kidney disease management.
problems: Acute on chronic systolic heart failure
Acute kidney failure with lesion of tubular necrosis
